title: Ethernet began as a way to connect nearby computers
body: On 22 May 1973, Robert Metcalfe wrote a memo at Xerox's research centre proposing Ethernet. Its early use was to connect computers and other devices such as printers on a local network.
takeaway: A network inside one building can serve a different purpose from a network that links cities.
source: Computer History Museum, Xerox Researcher Proposes Ethernet
visual: a cable connecting neighbouring early office computers on wooden desks

title: Rewriting Unix in C helped it travel between machines
body: At Bell Labs, Dennis Ritchie and colleagues developed C in the early 1970s and rewrote much of Unix in the language. The operating system relied less on instructions written for a particular processor.
takeaway: A language can make software easier to carry to new hardware without rebuilding it from the ground up.
source: Computer History Museum, Timeline of Computer History (1972)
visual: two differently shaped early computers linked by an unmarked reel of tape
